title: Cross-tenant clinical data disclosure
scenario: A user, API, worker, cache, export, object store, or admin route bypasses tenant authorization.
impact: Potential patient confidentiality breach and regulatory/contractual harm.
likelihood: UNKNOWN — assess after threat modelling and tests.
mitigation: Define trusted tenant context; enforce server/data-layer authorization; negative-test all resource paths; independent adversarial review.
notes: Initial risk hypothesis, not a confirmed vulnerability.

title: Clinical record wrong-patient or silent corruption
scenario: Identity ambiguity, concurrent update, migration error, or integration mapping associates or changes clinical data incorrectly.
impact: Potential patient harm, incorrect care decisions, or unrecoverable record inconsistency.
likelihood: UNKNOWN — assess with clinical safety analysis.
mitigation: Patient identity controls, provenance, append-only correction semantics, reconciliation, clinical scenario suite and hazard review.
notes: Initial risk hypothesis; scope depends on actual clinical workflows.

title: Unrecoverable or inconsistent data after failure
scenario: Backup is unusable, migration rollback fails, or recovery restores data without application-consistent state.
impact: Clinical/financial data loss and prolonged outage.
likelihood: UNKNOWN — no drill evidence supplied in architecture repo.
mitigation: Business-approved RTO/RPO; isolated restore drills; reconciliation; migration rehearsal; recovery/rollback evidence.
notes: Do not infer backup capability from a design statement.

title: Unsupported compliance claim
scenario: Architecture or marketing language claims legal compliance before jurisdiction-specific review and implementation evidence.
impact: Legal exposure, contract failure, loss of trust, or unlawful processing.
likelihood: UNKNOWN — verify claims against current docs and marketing.
mitigation: Trace obligation-to-control-to-test-to-evidence; obtain qualified jurisdiction review; constrain public claims.
notes: Risk scenario, not allegation of current non-compliance.

title: Design overrun before customer value is proven
scenario: Team implements broad target architecture without a triggered customer need or validated value.
impact: Schedule/cost overrun and reduced opportunity to validate product-market fit.
mitigation: Respect staged triggers; scope each phase; require measurable customer/user outcome and explicit exit criteria.
notes: Strategic risk hypothesis derived from staged implementation principle.

title: Evidence becomes stale after change
scenario: Tests/reviews refer to an old build, stack, law, partner profile, or configuration.
impact: False confidence and unsafe release decision.
likelihood: UNKNOWN — assess after evidence repository is active.
mitigation: Bind evidence to commit/build/config; expiry dates; trigger-based impact analysis; recurring evidence review.

title: Critical function unavailable under real load
scenario: Unmeasured concurrency, bottlenecks or dependency failures break patient-facing or staff-critical workflows.
impact: Delayed care/work, transactional backlog, or missed operational deadlines.
likelihood: UNKNOWN — workload profile and current implementation must be measured.
mitigation: Approved SLOs, representative load/stress/soak tests, dependency fault injection, alert/runbook readiness.
notes: Do not present architecture targets as measured capacity.
